title: Parallel tool calls: one batch of requests, executed together

events.label: Pose a comparison task
events.detail: "Which will be hotter tomorrow, Beijing or Shanghai?" — the two city queries do not depend on each other and naturally split into two requests.

events.label: Send the request
events.detail: The tool list holds a single get_weather(city, date) — how many requests the model emits in one reply is the model's own call.

events.label: Two tool_use blocks in one reply
events.detail: One reply carries two tool_use blocks: {"id":"toolu_bj1","name":"get_weather","input":{"city":"Beijing","date":"2026-09-07"}} and {"id":"toolu_sh2","name":"get_weather","input":{"city":"Shanghai","date":"2026-09-07"}}. Each has its own id; neither references the other.

events.label: Dependency check: independent → parallel
events.detail: One criterion only: does a later request need an earlier request's result to build its parameters? Here both city values are constants the model supplied directly — independent, so parallel is allowed.

events.label: Counter-example: dependencies force serialization
events.detail: If the task were "look up the city code first, then query the weather with it", the second request's parameters could not even be written before the first result returns — it must wait. Parallelism requires mutual independence, not merely looking like a batch.

events.label: Dispatch #1 (Beijing)
events.detail: Both queries go out at once — concurrent execution is the client's scheduling freedom; the model only requests and never knows how they run.

events.label: Dispatch #2 (Shanghai)
events.detail: In flight at the same moment as #1. Total latency becomes "the slowest of the two" instead of "both added together" — that is the whole latency win of parallelism.

events.label: Result #1 (Beijing: clear, 14–26°C)
events.detail: Completion order is not guaranteed; the fast one returns first. The client does not rush — it buffers by tool_use_id until all arrive.

events.label: Result #2 (Shanghai: cloudy, 18–28°C)
events.detail: Summarization starts only after both results are in — feeding back a partial set would let the model answer on incomplete observations.

events.label: Both tool_results replied together
events.detail: Two tool_result blocks (toolu_bj1 / toolu_sh2) are appended to messages, paired by id, and sent back in the same next request.

events.label: Summarize and answer
events.detail: The model compares the two observations: Shanghai's high of 28°C is hotter, plus a clothing suggestion. One summarizing call, no new tool requests.

events.label: Deliver the comparison
events.detail: The conclusion carries both raw query results. Total time ≈ one query's latency + two model calls, not twice the serial query latency.

events.label: Write the audit log
events.detail: Both tool_use/tool_result pairs are archived by id. In a concurrent world completion order scrambles; pairing by id is the anchor that keeps correctness.
